pr_title: [Windows] Override key codes with Unicode values for OEM keys only.
pr_body:
Should fix https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/101701 and still correctly process OEM keys (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/100960).

I was not able to fully test it since layouts from https://bepo.fr seems to be non-functional (crash explorer when you try to switch layout) and do not have physical JP106 keyboard.
pr_comments:
> With the BÉPO keyboard layout, since the 'U' key is located in the position of the physical 'S' key, it seems natural that the 'U' key would be input. However, I'm not familiar with French keyboards, so I support this PR.

This is not for regular BEPO, but for a special layout variant with physical 'S' key inputting `U` as text but `S` if `Ctrl` is pressed.
Thank you very much it saves my life !

issue_context.title: [4.4-beta.1] Editor reads keyboard inputs incorrectly when using uncommon Keyboard Layout BÉPO
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in : 4.4.beta1
- Not Reproducible in : 4.3.stable

### System information

Godot v4.4.beta1 - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6603) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-7600K CPU @ 3.80GHz (4 threads)

### Issue description

I use a uncommon keyboard layout on Windows called BÉPO [bepo-1.1rc2-full-azerty.exe](https://cdn.bepo.fr/windows/1.1rc2/bepo-1.1rc2-full-azerty.exe) that emulates shortcuts from the AZERTY layout, like Ctrl+S, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, etc.
My shortcuts now don't work anymore, which means I can't copy, paste, or save in the script editor using the correct shortcuts I use everywhere else and those shortcuts aren't editable so I can't rebind them.

Godot seems to have changed the way it reads input from Physical position to the letter that would give this position.
If I try to record the Save shortcut (Ctrl+S) on Godot4.3, it reads : 
"Ctrl+S or Ctrl+S (Physical) or Ctrl+U (Unicode)"
If I try the same on Godot4.4, it reads :
"**Ctrl+U** or Ctrl+S (Physical) or Ctrl+U (Unicode)"

### Steps to reproduce

Install AZERTY layout
Install the BÉPO layout [bepo-1.1rc2-full-azerty.exe](https://cdn.bepo.fr/windows/1.1rc2/bepo-1.1rc2-full-azerty.exe) (the one using AZERTY shortcuts)
Open Godot4.4 and navigate towards Editor > Editor Settings > Shortcuts
Try to bind shortcuts that use the Ctrl key in both layouts
Notice it's not the same (when it's the same in Godot4.3)

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A
comments:
> "Ctrl+U or Ctrl+S (Physical) or Ctrl+U (Unicode)"

This seems exactly how it should be, for basic Latin `keycode` and `unicode` should always match.

Do you mean Godot just got what's expected and it wasn't previously the case ?
Then the fault is in BÉPO or it's just a doomed issue ?
In any case, if this change is here to stay, then people like me will need the option to rebind the Script Editor "basic" shortcuts.
It would also be great if I could just ask Godot to consider all my shortcuts Physical so I don't have to rebind everything.

This what feels expected to me, but I'm not sure if I understand how this layout is working, is it supposed to have the same physical key to emit `Ctrl+S` but input `U` as text?

The change is likely caused by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/100960, and it was added to fix some OEM keys, but change work on the whole ASCII character range, we probably can restrict it to only special characters and still have both OEM keys and this working.

Yes basically, where there's an S in AZERTY, it now outputs an U in BÉPO. But when I press Ctrl + the key at that position, it still is supposed to give me Ctrl+S, so that the shortcuts don't move between AZERTY and BÉPO.

review_comments: Since it's already restricted to OEM keys, I think ASCII range restriction may not be necessary.
Unlikely it will be ever outside this range, but there's no exact list of the valid values OEM keys can produce, and `keycode` still expected to be limited to 102-key US QWERTY keyboard values.
Sure I think it would be better to keep the ASCII range restriction for safety.
